result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md, closing the BLOCKER CODE-DESIGNER filed against its own step-01-code-designer.json handoff: this run's Step 1 dispatch had named only CODE-DESIGNER, leaving REQ-019.md Sec1's schema gap unspecified. Read REQ-019.md in full first to derive the exact shape determineNextProfileField (Sec2.2) needs from the schema, then REQ-010's current profiles table (apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts:97-126), then REQ-014-schema.md/REQ-016-schema.md as this role's own precedent for column-naming, nullability-justification, migration-prose, and S11/S13 reasoning style, then decisions/0005-orm-drizzle.md for the Drizzle-generated-migration convention and security-invariants.md S11/S13 for the redaction/anonymization gates.

Two changes designed, both against the existing profiles table only, no new table:

1. Relax NOT NULL on first_name, last_name, company, position, is_student, experience_level (all six, including first_name -- accepting REQ-019.md Sec1's own recommendation for a uniform completeness predicate, though only the other five are strictly forced by AC1). No CHECK constraint re-imposes eventual completeness -- isProfileComplete (REQ-019.md Sec2.3) is the sole authority on that from this point on, an application-level invariant, not a database one, since no acceptance criterion asks the DB to guarantee eventual completion and a CHECK cannot express 'eventually set' regardless. Confirmed by inspecting every other in-flight design doc (REQ-014/016/017/018) that nothing else reads these six columns' nullability directly, so nothing else is blocked.

2. Add five new booleans -- phone_skipped, email_skipped, links_github_skipped, links_linkedin_skipped, links_site_skipped -- each NOT NULL DEFAULT false. Chose five plain booleans over CODE-DESIGNER's other named option (a combined JSONB/array column) because: the optional-field set is fixed and closed at exactly five (named by the requirement's own text, not organizer-configurable or variable-length, unlike events.agenda's genuinely variable JSONB shape), this schema's own established convention for a small closed set of per-row facts is one boolean column per fact (is_student, publish_consent, blocked, broadcast_opt_in -- no existing table uses a JSONB/array column for a fixed named-flag set), a plain boolean is directly exportable/absorbable by a future platform with zero JSON-decoding step (per this role's own 'exportable and absorbable' rule), and it matches ProfileRecord's own one-property-per-column shape (REQ-019.md Sec2.2) with no serialize/deserialize step and no risk of a silently-mistyped array entry. NOT NULL DEFAULT false (not nullable) for the same two-valued-fact reasoning REQ-014-schema.md Sec1 applied to chapters.active -- a third NULL state would need special-casing determineNextProfileField's step 2 check for no benefit, and DEFAULT false means the very first INSERT (bare firstName) needs no explicit value for any of the five.

Migration: Drizzle-generated per decisions/0005 (BACKEND-DEV runs drizzle-kit generate against an updated schema.ts, never hand-written) -- 6 ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL statements plus 5 ADD COLUMN ... boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false statements, all against the single existing profiles table, no backfill script needed (DROP NOT NULL touches no data; ADD COLUMN...DEFAULT backfills atomically in the same ALTER TABLE, same pattern as REQ-014-schema.md's chapters.active). Reversibility stated honestly: dropping the five skip columns is a clean, if lossy, reversal (same class as REQ-016-schema.md's pending_source); re-adding NOT NULL to any of the six required columns is NOT unconditionally reversible once a genuine in-progress signup row exists at rollback time -- flagged explicitly, mirroring REQ-014-schema.md Sec11's identical caveat for consent_pd_at/consent_pd_version.

S11: no new PII-bearing column -- the five new columns are content-free booleans, and phone/email's own nullability is untouched. S13: DROP NOT NULL is a widening, not a drop-or-rewrite of column content, so it does not trigger S13/decisions-0005 sign-off (stated explicitly as a first-instance clarification for future NOT-NULL-relaxation migrations on PII columns, since S13 gates the opposite operation). No CHECK constraint is added forbidding a value column being non-null while its skip flag is true -- REQ-019.md Sec2.4's write-path discipline (answering un-skips atomically) already prevents the combination, and adding DB enforcement of an application-guaranteed state is unrequested machinery (same restraint REQ-016-schema.md Sec6 already exercised) -- filed as open question 1 in case SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR wants it added anyway.

Added a one-line 'Resolved' cross-reference in docs/agents/design/REQ-019.md's own Sec1 pointing to the new schema doc and confirming ProfileRecord's shape matches -- no other edit to CODE-DESIGNER's design.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md Sec10 open question 1: no CHECK constraint forbids a value column being non-null while its matching *_skipped flag is true. Declined as unrequested DB-level enforcement of a state the application write-path (REQ-019.md Sec2.4) already prevents, consistent with REQ-016-schema.md Sec6's identical restraint. Flagged for SECURITY-REVIEWER/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to confirm or override, not resolved by invention here.

docs/agents/design/REQ-019-schema.md Sec10 open question 2: relaxing first_name's NOT NULL (alongside the other five) is this artefact's own uniformity recommendation, accepted from REQ-019.md Sec1, not strictly forced by any acceptance criterion. Recorded for the record in case a future review prefers keeping first_name NOT NULL.
